target.name: AheadComputing
target.founder: Debbie Marr, Mark Dechene, Jonathan Pearce, Srikanth Srinivasan

methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Seed → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.5x) to $52M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Chips & Semiconductors (found 0 same-stage, 1 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 12 same-sector peers exist in Chips & Semiconductors, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

methods.name: Public-Comp Anchoring
methods.skip_reason: target revenue not on file (private companies rarely disclose)
methods.rationale: Public Semiconductors P/S median is 21.4x across 3 tickers. Cannot apply without target's revenue.

data.narrative:
AheadComputing is a Seed-stage semiconductor company founded by Marr, Dechene, Pearce, and Srinivasan that has raised $51.5M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a comp universe of 3 public semiconductors (ALAB, NVDA, AMD) and 8 private peers including Cerebras, Credo Semiconductor, and SambaNova Systems.

Of three valuation methods evaluated, only Stage-Progression proved applicable. Using total capital raised ($51.5M) as a proxy for current value and applying a 2.5x multiplier typical of Seed-to-Series A progression yields $129M. This single-method result establishes the median point. Peer-Median analysis could not proceed due to insufficient same-stage and adjacent-stage comparables within the narrow Chips & Semiconductors category—while 12 same-sector peers exist, none met clustering thresholds. Public-Comp Anchoring proved inapplicable because AheadComputing's revenue is not disclosed; the public semiconductor median P/S of 21.4x cannot be deployed without this input.

The triangulated range is $109M (low) to $148M (high), centered at $129M. This valuation depends almost entirely on the stage-progression assumption, introducing material uncertainty. Key limitations include reliance on a single method, the lack of revenue-scaled public comparables, and sparse private peer data at identical stage and valuation tier. Revenue disclosure or additional Seed-stage private comp data would materially strengthen conviction in this range.
